orbits.titel: Five orbits, one core business. Isar’s open market lies almost entirely in sun-synchronous orbit.
orbits.titel_fern: Key focus is to strengthen our core, Launch as a Service.
orbits.titel_aussen: Key focus stays on our core. Other models are possible on the platform, but we do not pursue them.
orbits.hinweis: Click an orbit or a satellite
orbits.fuss_fern: We focus on the nucleus to strengthen our core first. Market size: launch services market 2025.
orbits.fuss_aussen: Planets of the solar system = other business models, area = market potential in USD B (case DB business_models; telecom and satellite services from SIA 2025). Orbit = proximity to the core (near, mid, far). All possible on top of the launch platform, none of them pursued: focus stays on the nucleus. Models without a market figure in the DB are not shown.
orbits.quelle: Satellites and mass 2025 by inclination, engine funnel and GCAT. Mass = all satellites in the orbit.

bahnen.label: Equatorial to GEO
bahnen.name: Equatorial to GEO
bahnen.isar: only from Kourou, up to 1,000 kg
bahnen.text: Hardly any market for a 1 t rocket: GEO satellites are too heavy and too high for Spectrum.

bahnen.label: Mid 40–60°
bahnen.name: Mid inclination
bahnen.isar: from Nova Scotia (850 kg), Kourou or Santa Maria
bahnen.text: The largest orbit, but 85% Starlink. 44 remain open, mostly educational cubesats. Future: IRIS² and the LEO initiative.

bahnen.label: High 60–80°
bahnen.name: High inclination
bahnen.isar: only from Nova Scotia, SaxaVord, Kourou or Santa Maria
bahnen.text: Volume yes, open market no: Starlink launches almost all of it itself.

bahnen.label: Polar 80–95°
bahnen.name: Polar
bahnen.text: Technically close, but hardly any open market: the rest is Chinese, captive or unsuitable.

bahnen.label: SSO 95–100° · Isar core
bahnen.name: Sun-synchronous (SSO)
bahnen.text: Almost the entire open market sits here: 405 of the 406 openly addressable satellites from Andøya.

Wage = Eurostat labour cost per hour in industry 2025 (ES, DE). *Estimates: UK from ONS ASHE 2026 (air and spacecraft, GBP 30.03 gross) × 1.19; Canada aerospace parts, wages only, CAD 38.93 (StatCan 2024).

modell.formel: Investment = factories × value per factory + pads × cost per pad. Pads = what it takes to fly every rocket the factories build.
hebel: share of design capacity that is built and flown
unpublished, Vaterstetten is leased from VGP; proxy Rocket Lab Long Beach USD 16M bought, about USD 100M replacement
modell.check_hoch: Cross-check: {need} rockets a year, but only {win} missions are winnable for Isar in 2030 (case DB). Closing {pct} of the world gap needs market access beyond today’s open market. That is the hypothesis to test.
modell.check_tief: Cross-check: at this setting production stays below what Isar can win today ({win} missions in 2030). The constraint is the break-even of {be} launches, not the market.

Launch right and pad for Isar [gap]
